data.title: Anthropic IPO to mint thousands of millionaires
data.description: NEW YORK, Nov 18 : Anthropic's initial public offering is poised to create thousands of paper millionaires among current and former employees, in what could rank among the largest employee wealth windfalls in Silicon Valley history.   The offering is expected to unleash a wave of new wealth across the AI sector, rewarding everyone from early researchers and engineers to administrative staff who received stock grants as the Claude maker raced from startup to one of the world's most valuable companies. The IPO filing shows the amount of wealth embedded in employee stock awards, but not how that wealth is distributed among workers. As a result, outside estimates vary widely. Hill, a San Francisco marketplace for private-company shares, estimates 598 non-founder employees will hold at least $100 million in equity after the initial public offering, which is slated to open on the Nasdaq on Thursday at $83 a share, above its initial target range that would value the company at up to $1.4 trillion, according to a person familiar with the information. Private-markets research firm Sacra estimates that roughly 2,800 current and former Anthropic employees could hold at least $1 million of pretax vested equity at a $1.35 trillion valuation, the middle of the price range.  The firms say their estimates are model-based and use public information. Reuters could not independently verify the estimates, which reflect factors including vesting periods, exercises, tender transactions, option awards, restricted stock units, award timing, headcount and employee retention rates. The filing does not disclose sums due individuals. But the wealth potentially shared by employees is vast.  Anthropic option holders were sitting on $119 billion of paper gains as of September 30, at a weighted average exercise price of $2.91 per share, the company disclosed. About $73 billion of that amount had vested through service and could be exercised immediately.  Anthropic did not respond to a comment request on the estimates. "The idea of equity appreciating to an amount that is life-changing is something that people strive for," Hill CEO Andrew Benson said. "It doesn't get better than this." EQUITY AT ENTRY LEVEL Workers who joined the firm when it started five years ago —  even in administrative positions and entry-level jobs — could be sitting on life-changing wealth, reflecting their holdings of stock options that carry exercise prices of less than $1.  Options granted through 2023 and still outstanding at the end of that year carried an average exercise price of 52 cents, the filing shows.  At SpaceX, which was founded in 2002 and went  public in June in a record-busting IPO, many of the employees who became millionaires had worked there for more than a decade.    "Early employees who started in a very junior role should have actually a better financial outcome than somebody who joined in a very senior role right before the IPO," Benson said, referring to Anthropic. Non-founder Anthropic employees can sell up to 10 per cent of their holdings on the first trading day, and up to another 35 per cent after fiscal 2026 earnings. EARLY HIRES REAP REWARDS Founded in 2021, the Claude maker expanded its workforce rapidly alongside the AI boom, growing to about 5,300 employees as of September 30 from roughly 940 at the end of 2024. As it hired aggressively, the company used stock-based compensation as a key recruiting tool. A May 2024 job posting for an administrative business partner role shows how the benefits of Anthropic's stock awards extended beyond AI researchers and engineers.  The position, which involved scheduling and managing calendars for company leaders, coordinating conference logistics and handling expense claims and reimbursements, paid an annual salary of $140,000 to $190,000.  The posting added that equity would be "a major component of the total compensation" beyond the salary, indicating that administrative and support staff were also eligible for stock awards alongside cash pay. That year, Anthropic said it granted employees options at an average exercise price of $1.30 per share. "And as we know from several anecdotes after the SpaceX IPO, this is often enough to help people down the organization chart do quite well in IPO," said Marcelo Ballve, head of research at Sacra. Anthropic granted CFO Krishna Rao 14 million stock options in 2024, also with a $1.30 exercise price, according to the filing. At the IPO price range, those options would carry roughly $1 billion in gross intrinsic value, before exercise costs and taxes. Ballve said that equity awards for administrative, support and entry-level roles are not uncommon at venture capital-backed companies. Historically, though, many companies phased out equity grants at hiring for these roles as they scaled up and salaries became more competitive, moving to performance- and tenure-based grants instead. After Anthropic goes public, the company will likely reserve upfront equity grants solely for recruiting top talent, he said.

data.title: Palo Alto raises annual forecast, signs $4.5 billion deal for Applied Compute
data.description: Nov 18 : Cybersecurity firm Palo Alto Networks raised its annual revenue forecast and signed a deal to acquire AI startup Applied Compute in a deal valued at $4.5 billion, as a heightened threat environment pushes customers toward broader security products. Shares of Palo Alto jumped about 10 per cent in after-hours trading to $368.60, and drove gains in rivals. CrowdStrike rose 5.3 per cent, Zscaler climbed 3 per cent and Fortinet gained 2.1 per cent. Palo Alto Networks has been repositioning itself as an integrated cybersecurity provider, with recent deals, including its $3.35 billion acquisition of cloud management and monitoring firm Chronosphere and an agreement with Israeli startup Koi. The company is looking to tap growing cybersecurity spending as the rapid adoption of AI creates new security risks, giving attackers new ways to exploit vulnerabilities. "As AI accelerates cyber attacks, enterprises are moving with urgency to replace disjointed tools with unified platforms," Palo Alto CEO Nikesh Arora said during the company's analyst call on Wednesday. With the acquisition of Applied Compute, Palo Alto is looking to offer users a technology platform to help customers securely train and deploy open-weight models as they expand their use of AI. Open-weight models, AI systems whose trained settings are publicly released, present security challenges, including the risk of model tampering, data leakage and misuse by bad actors. "Applied Compute extends Palo Alto's push beyond traditional cybersecurity into enterprise AI. The opportunity is to bring AI infrastructure and security closer together," said Shaul Eyal, analyst at TD Cowen. The deal is expected to close in the third quarter of fiscal 2027. Palo Alto now expects fiscal 2027 revenue to be between $14.52 billion and $14.57 billion, compared with its prior expectation of $14.10 billion to $14.20 billion. Its first-quarter revenue came in at $3.45 billion, up 39 per cent from a year earlier, beating estimates of $3.31 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG.

data.title: Stocks slip with eyes on Anthropic and Nvidia, oil prices slide
data.description: NEW YORK/LONDON, Nov 18 : A gauge of stocks across the globe fell on Wednesday after Nvidia's quarterly results and ahead of Anthropic's market debut, while the dollar's strength on the back of a hawkish Federal Reserve weighed on trader sentiment. The dollar index strengthened to a fresh 19-month high after US Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller told CNBC the central bank needs to either approve a half-point interest rate hike at its December meeting or communicate a faster pace of hikes in 2027. Mining stocks dragged European shares lower, while Nvidia's results initially helped Asian shares, with South Korea's Kospi up 2 per cent overnight. But the Nvidia rally fizzled and its stock fell 2.9 per cent after rising as much as 2.7 per cent. Nvidia's board dismissed the idea of rehiring former CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned last week. The company's results and strong outlook did not dispel uncertainty. "We believe (Tuesday's) results have stabilized sentiment and put a floor under the recent AI selloff, but they have postponed rather than permanently cured investor anxiety," said Neil Shah, vice president of research at Counterpoint. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.11 per cent to 50,198.17, the S&P 500 lost 0.23 per cent to 7,323.63 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.42 per cent to 24,429.89.  MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe fell 0.45 per cent to 1,074.61. The pan-European STOXX 600 index fell 1.03 per cent, while emerging market stocks fell 0.2 per cent. Japan's Nikkei rose 0.28 per cent to 59,024.28. The next health check on the AI industry will come as Anthropic prepares its market debut on Thursday. The company priced its initial public offering on Wednesday at $83 per share, above the expected range, according to a person familiar with the matter. DOLLAR UP, OIL DOWN In currencies, the dollar strengthened as Waller's comments and recent economic data cemented expectations for an interest rate hike next month. "The Federal Reserve seems at the moment to be very determined to hike interest rates and maybe even aggressively do so," said Juan Perez, senior director of trading at Monex USA in Washington. "That's the belief right now that's carrying the US dollar." The dollar index rose 0.17 per cent to 103.79, with the euro down 0.22 per cent at $1.0973. In commodities markets, crude prices fell after US crude and fuel inventories rose more than expected, adding to expectations of a supply surplus.  US crude lost 3.3 per cent to $83.17 a barrel and Brent fell to $91.84 per barrel, down 1.4 per cent. Spot gold dropped 3.24 per cent to $3,725.10 an ounce and spot silver fell 4.98 per cent to $45.04 an ounce. Copper declined 4.54 per cent to $12,626.00 a ton. Yields on 2-year US Treasury notes, which are sensitive to interest rate expectations, edged higher on hawkish Fed speaker comments and minutes from the last monetary policy committee meeting that underscored inflation worries. The 2-year note yield rose 1.31 basis points to 4.802 per cent, from 4.789 per cent late on Tuesday, while the benchmark US 10-year note yield fell 3.47 basis points to 5.068 per cent, from 5.103 per cent.

data.title: Anthropic prices blockbuster IPO at $83 a share, source says
data.description: Nov 18 : Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 a share, above its targeted range of $70 to $78 per share on Wednesday, in one of the largest stock-market IPOs on record and the first by a major frontier artificial intelligence model developer, according to a person familiar with the matter. The size of the offering has increased, the person said, asking not to be identified because the information isn’t public. The pricing makes Anthropic's sale the second mega-IPO of the year with a focus on AI, following June's SpaceX sale, as investors jump at the chance for exposure to the fast-growing industry, even as the industry also faces mounting questions over the cost of developing and operating artificial intelligence models. The AI lab comes to the public market just months after SpaceX's record-setting IPO, but the backdrop for AI stocks has turned more challenging. Chipmakers and cloud companies central to the business have come under pressure in recent weeks due to valuation concerns, mounting AI infrastructure costs, and the sudden resignation of Jensen Huang as CEO of chipmaker Nvidia, a key pillar of the industry's growth.  The pricing follows a roadshow that attracted demand exceeding several multiples of the number of shares offered, Reuters previously reported, despite questions about the company's outlook and its ability to sustain rapid growth as competition in the AI industry intensifies. Anthropic's closest rival, OpenAI, is also expected to pursue a public listing as early as next year. Anthropic declined to comment.  Bloomberg news first reported on the pricing.

data.title: Palo Alto to buy AI startup Applied Compute for $4.5 billion
data.description: Nov 18 : Cybersecurity company Palo Alto Networks said on Wednesday it will acquire AI startup Applied Compute in an all-stock deal valued at $4.5 billion, as it seeks to help businesses securely deploy open-weight artificial intelligence models. Shares of Palo Alto rose 8.5 per cent in after hours trading. The latest deal adds to a run of 2026 acquisitions by Palo Alto, including identity-security company CyberArk and observability firm Chronosphere, as the company pushes into AI. Applied Compute sells software that helps companies adapt and run open-weight models, AI systems whose trained settings are publicly released, on their own data. The deal is expected to close in the third quarter of fiscal 2027. Separately, Palo Alto said it expects fiscal 2027 revenue to be between $14.52 billion and $14.57 billion, above analysts' average estimate of $14.16 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG.

data.title: UAE Court orders freeze on crypto tokens stolen from Binance wallets
data.description: PARIS, Nov 18 : Crypto exchange Binance said it had secured a court order from Abu Dhabi Global Markets – its main financial regulator – as part of its efforts to recover funds which were frozen after hackers stole $6.3 billion worth of crypto last month. Binance has previously said that around $2.85 billion worth of the stolen crypto tokens had been frozen or intercepted by third parties after the hack. “We will continue using every lawful tool available to trace, freeze and recover stolen assets, support our partners in returning funds where possible, and keep those assets out of the hands of the attackers,” Dugan Bliss, deputy general counsel at Binance, said in a statement on Wednesday.

data.title: Surge in software patches likely behind recent tech outages, experts say
data.description: Nov 18 : While the causes of recent disruptions to the way people work, access bank accounts and travel remain unclear, increased efforts to rapidly patch newly discovered vulnerabilities in the AI age are likely a major factor, according to cybersecurity experts and US officials. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, speaking to reporters in Manila this week, said company patching efforts are, at times, "creating short-term disruption in the way the system works." Patches are software and operating system updates intended to fix security vulnerabilities found within a program or product. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told a House of Representatives Homeland Security Committee hearing on worldwide threats Wednesday that there is so far no indication that the tech outages are related. But Clayton said the speed and level of capability of computer systems are "increasing substantially," so legacy computer systems and equipment that already were old are aging much more quickly. The advent of easily accessible AI tools and large language models has supercharged the discovery of vulnerabilities in software. Microsoft this month has addressed more than 1,200 software vulnerabilities, nearly 20 times higher than in the same month a year ago, according to cybersecurity firm Qualys. At least one major bank was rushing to address a wave of recent patches and there is a lot of work needed, a source at the bank said, speaking on condition of anonymity.  "AI has made finding critical vulnerabilities fast and cheap, and the number of flaws that demand immediate patching has grown with it," said Yuval Itzchakov, CTO and co-founder of autonomous offensive security company A Security.  "Emergency patches go into core infrastructure within hours, often without the full testing cycle, and they are intrusive by design: they change runtimes, kernels and network components that everything else depends on. That speed and scale of change is itself a source of failure," Itzchakov said. Josh Bressers, director of coordinated vulnerability disclosure at cybersecurity firm VulnCheck, said that in 2026 there have been 100,000 publicly disclosed vulnerabilities, tracked by industry as Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures, or CVEs. Of those, Bressers said, 1,363 were known to have been exploited in the real world.  "Given tight resources for defenders, understanding which vulnerabilities need attention first is critical," Bressers wrote in a LinkedIn post. "Not all vulnerabilities are created equal." Anne Neuberger, general partner at Andreessen Horowitz, said that AI is helping attackers find and weaponize vulnerabilities, but is a more "valuable friend" to those tasked with defending key computer networks. "AI is enabling enterprises to find 10 times more vulnerabilities," said Neuberger, who served as deputy national security adviser under former President Joe Biden and led incident response to serious national incidents. "And when patching at scale, some can cause problems." Ronald Gestiehr, director of wealth management at Luttner Financial, said technology has made banking "incredibly convenient, and while occasional outages can be frustrating I don't believe the outages will have a significant impact on consumer confidence or change how most people manage their money."  "Financial institutions have invested heavily in technology and security, and, unfortunately, occasional disruptions will happen," Gestiehr said. "What matters most is how quickly those issues are identified, resolved and communicated to customers."

data.title: GTA VI frenzy spotlights potential insurance risks lurking in digital infrastructure
data.description: Nov 18 : Millions of gamers around the world have logged on for the launch of "Grand Theft Auto VI," arguably the century's most anticipated video game, offering a glimpse of the vast, interconnected digital infrastructure the global economy increasingly relies on. No major disruption is expected from the rollout. But the scale of demand around one of the gaming industry's biggest releases underscores a broader risk for insurers: a failure at a shared cloud, payments or technology provider could affect thousands of businesses at once. After 13 years in development and an estimated $1 billion or more in production costs, 'Grand Theft Auto VI' began rolling out globally on Thursday, drawing the kind of attention that few entertainment releases ever command. But the fervour also underscores how much modern businesses depend on the digital infrastructure that makes such mass online activity possible, and the risks insurers face when that infrastructure fails. "A launch of the scale of GTA VI is effectively a built-in stress test of the shared digital economy infrastructure," said Marcos Alvarez, managing director at Morningstar DBRS. Insurers cover businesses against financial losses stemming from disruptions to their operations, including some caused by technology failures. As companies increasingly rely on the same cloud providers, payment systems and digital platforms, a single outage could trigger claims from multiple policyholders at once, amplifying exposure. Despite the frenzy surrounding the launch, any disruption on launch day or in the days that follow would not necessarily spell disaster for insurers, industry experts said. "The recent technology outages have been a case in point with the gap between the economic cost and the actual insured loss being quite large due to policy limits, retentions, waiting periods, and coverage exclusions," Alvarez added. Business interruption could be a major source of claims, but coverage could also extend to costs associated with data recovery, system restoration, cyberattacks and outages at third-party technology providers, depending on the policy. "This is an area that is evolving rapidly for the insurance industry. Insurers are refining how they assess, model and manage these interconnected exposures," said Loretta Worters, a spokesperson for the Insurance Information Institute. "That means looking beyond an individual company's cybersecurity protections to understand its reliance on third-party providers, the concentration of those dependencies across their portfolios and the potential for a single event to generate losses across multiple policyholders." ​

US Treasury yields were slightly lower as oil prices dropped, dragging inflation expectations lower. The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes fell 3.87 basis points to 5.064 per cent from 5.103 per cent late on Tuesday, while the 30-year bond yield fell 4.49 basis points to 5.414 per cent from 5.459 per cent.

data.title: Texas resumes issuing data center air permits, regulator says
data.description: NEW YORK, Nov 18 : Texas has resumed issuing air permits for data centers, state regulators said on Wednesday, after pausing the practice last month as part of the state's broader attempt to manage the server warehouses and their effects on the electrical grid, communities and the environment. • The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality "has resumed its normal permit review process and will evaluate applications under all applicable state and federal laws and regulations," TCEQ spokesperson Laura Lopez said. • Texas Governor Greg Abbott halted the connection of new data centers to the state electric grid in August and ordered an audit of the projects, rattling one of the world's fastest-growing hubs for data center development. Abbott followed up by temporarily blocking air permits for all data center projects. • The air permit resumption came after the Texas grid operator notified the TCEQ that it had collected "community impact review" information for proposed data center projects, Lopez said. • Abbott, a Republican, lost his reelection bid in this month's midterm elections to Democratic challenger Gina Hinojosa, who has promised to impose a moratorium on data centers once in office in January. • The most recent permitting decision may generate more pushback from incoming Texas Democratic lawmakers and politicians in the new year, analysts said. • "TD Cowen sees Abbott's lame duck permitting push as likely to strengthen the Dem-stakeholder demand that Hinojosa take a firm stand, reducing hopes for a near-term policy agreement between Hinojosa and data center developers," the firm said in a note.

data.description: PARIS, Nov 18 : Crypto exchange Binance said it had secured a court order from Abu Dhabi Global Markets – its main financial regulator – as part of its efforts to recover funds which were frozen after hackers stole $6.3 billion worth of crypto last month. Binance has previously said that around $2.85 billion worth of the stolen crypto tokens had been frozen or intercepted by third parties after the hack. “We will continue using every lawful tool available to trace, freeze and recover stolen assets, support our partners in returning funds where possible, and keep those assets out of the hands of the attackers,” Dugan Bliss, deputy general counsel at Binance, said in a statement on Wednesday.

data.title: Anthropic options could begin trading on Monday, expected to draw strong demand
data.description: NEW YORK, Nov 18 : Options on Anthropic shares could begin trading as soon as Monday, giving investors a new way to wager on the AI company's prospects as market participants expect heavy interest. Cboe Global Markets expects to list the contracts two business days after the stock begins trading, pending industry readiness. “The Anthropic IPO could be yet another catalyst, bringing a new wave of investors and trading activity to the options market," said Rob Hocking, Cboe’s global head of derivatives. "It’s great to see investor education driving this growth, as more people learn how options let them define their risk. An exciting trend and one we expect to continue.”  The Claude developer is expected to price its IPO later on Wednesday, and the shares will begin trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday.   "We expect significant interest in Anthropic options once they list," said Garrett DeSimone, head quant at OptionMetrics. "The combination of AI-driven enthusiasm and the lottery-like payoff profile typical of IPOs are likely to draw investors immediately. As one of the most concentrated pure-play exposures to AI, the stock is also likely to be highly volatile." Interest in Anthropic options could exceed the interest in SpaceX options earlier this year, said Ophir Gottlieb, chief executive of Capital Market Laboratories, citing oversubscription that is pushing the company's valuation higher and could invite various positioning ahead of the deal, as well as the market backdrop. "The AI trade is melting down," Gottlieb said. "Many feel it is overdone, while many others feel it's the popping of a bubble. Whenever there is such opposing views in a heated market, we get a lot of option positioning." Options give holders the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell shares at a set price within a certain period. They offer investors a cheaper way to gain exposure to a stock and to express their views on both short-term price moves and longer-term positioning. Anthropic’s $64 billion IPO has drawn stronger early institutional demand than the offering of SpaceX, with the book six times oversubscribed last week, Reuters previously reported. The IPO has drawn anticipation from investors, with Wall Street rolling out products tied to the stock, hosting client events and giving away merchandise ahead of the AI company's potentially record launch.

data.title: 'GTA VI' publisher Take-Two jumps as gamers relish blockbuster release
data.description: Nov 18 : As "Grand Theft Auto VI" begins its global rollout on Wednesday, gamers and critics are applauding the blockbuster release. And so is Wall Street.  Shares of Take-Two Interactive, the owner of the studio behind GTA VI, jumped more than 6 per cent in premarket trading, with investors betting that glowing reviews from critics and players will propel sales and boost the company's bookings and revenue this year. Demand has been feverish - with players doing everything from taking several days of paid time off to signing "contracts" with their partners to get uninterrupted game time. Here are more details on the expected revenue impact for Take-Two: • Wells Fargo expects GTA VI to sell about 65 million units in its current fiscal year that runs through March, up from its prior forecast of 35 million units • The brokerage's estimate is also boosted by expectations for a potential PC release of the game early in 2027 • It lifted its annual bookings forecast by 19 per cent to $9.76 billion, versus a consensus estimate of $8 billion from LSEG data, and Take-Two's own projection of $8 billion to $8.20 billion • Brokerage Oppenheimer estimates about $1.85 billion in gross revenue in the first three days, compared with the $1 billion recorded by predecessor GTA V, released more than 13 years ago • A Sensor Tower tracker estimates roughly 17.1 million units have been sold as of early Wednesday, far exceeding pre-order volumes of all the biggest game releases in recent history

data.title: Stocks slip as investors mull Nvidia earnings; Anthropic IPO to test AI boom
data.description: LONDON, Nov 18 : World stocks struggled on Wednesday, as investors digested Nvidia's better-than-expected sales forecast and braced for Anthropic's market debut, seen as a major test of the AI investment boom.  MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe fell 0.1 per cent, with European shares losing 0.2 per cent and bourses in Frankfurt , Paris and London all declining, the latter dragged down by rising UK inflation.  It nevertheless represented a semblance of steadiness for European equities after they suffered their biggest one-day decline in eight months on Tuesday. European tech stocks rose 1.3 per cent, with heavyweight chip-equipment maker ASML rising 3.6 per cent. Top of the agenda for investors was AI chip company Nvidia, which on Tuesday gave a better-than-expected sales forecast amid uncertainty about the company's future leadership. Its chairman told investors the AI chip company would not rehire co-founder Jensen Huang, widely seen as the face of the AI boom, as CEO. Wall Street was also set for gains, with S&P 500 e-mini futures gaining 0.4 per cent. Nasdaq 100 E-minis were up 0.9 per cent.On Tuesday, US stocks had sold off, with the S&P 500 down 1 per cent to log a fourth straight loss prior to Nvidia's earnings report.  "Nvidia is an AI bellwether and a lot of people pay attention to what they guide, what they say in terms of their demand," said Fleura Shiyanova, an equity analyst at Kepler Unigestion in Switzerland. "Anything they decide to change will go through various value chains within the AI theme."   In oil markets, Brent crude futures trimmed losses to stand 0.7 per cent lower at $92.70 a barrel following data showing an increase in US crude and fuel inventories last week, although the ongoing Middle East conflict and disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz limited losses. 'REFERENDUM ON AI' Nvidia's results helped Asian shares outside Japan eke out a slim gain of 0.1 per cent to break a four-day losing streak. Japan's Nikkei 225 gained 0.3 per cent after several reversals. The next health check on the AI industry will come as Anthropic prepares to price its shares later on Wednesday ahead of its initial public offering, which could value the company at as much as $1.4 trillion. The company has guided its IPO price to the top of its range or above, Bloomberg News reported.  "I’ve looked at this whole week as a referendum on AI," said Jake Behan, head of capital markets at Direxion in New York. "Nvidia gave us a read on the buildout, and Anthropic is about to give us a read on investor appetite for the next generation of AI companies." In currency markets, the US dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was up 0.2 per cent at 103.78, after earlier reaching its highest level on Tuesday since President Donald Trump's announcement of tariffs in April 2025. The euro hit its latest low since April 2025, and was last down 0.3 per cent at $1.096. In choppy trading, the yen last stood flat against the US dollar at 159.30 yen. Data showed Japan's exports rose for a 14th successive month in October, driven by demand for shipments related to semiconductors.  The yield on the US 10-year Treasury bond was down 0.6 basis point at 5.095 per cent. On Tuesday, St Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem, who is a non-voter on interest rates this year, said that the Federal Reserve may need several rate hikes to bring inflation under control and should act soon to ensure the problem doesn't get worse. British government bond yields fell after inflation data showed a somewhat softer picture than economists and the Bank of England had been expecting, causing investors to scale back bets slightly on a December rate rise.
